title: Enums and Pattern Matching
description: Master BPL's powerful enum system and pattern matching. Create algebraic data types and handle all cases elegantly.
objectives: Define enums with and without associated data
Use pattern matching with match expressions

sections.title: What are Enums?
sections.content:
An **enum** (enumeration) is a type that can be one of several **variants**.

Simple example:
```bpl
enum Direction {
    North, South, East, West
}
```

BPL enums are **algebraic data types** - variants can hold data:
```bpl
enum Option<T> {
    Some(T),   # Has a value
    None       # No value
}
```

This makes them perfect for representing states, results, and optional values.

sections.title: Pattern Matching Rules
sections.content:
**Pattern matching must be exhaustive** - handle all variants!

```bpl
enum Status { Active, Inactive, Pending }

match (status) {
    Status.Active => ...,
    Status.Inactive => ...,
    # Error! Missing Status.Pending
}
```

**Use wildcard `_` for catch-all:**
```bpl
match (status) {
    Status.Active => printf("Active!"),
    _ => printf("Not active"),  # Matches anything else
}
```

The compiler ensures you handle all cases, preventing bugs!

sections.title: Practice: Expression Evaluator
sections.instructions:
Create an enum `Expr` with variants:
- `Num(int)` - a number
- `Add(int, int)` - addition
- `Mul(int, int)` - multiplication

Write an `evaluate(expr: Expr) ret int` function that computes the result.
sections.hint: Use match to handle each variant and perform the appropriate operation.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **Enums** represent one of several possible variants

✅ Variants can hold **associated data** of any type

✅ **match** expressions handle each variant

✅ Pattern matching **extracts data** from variants

✅ **Option<T>** represents optional values (Some/None)

✅ **Result<T, E>** represents success/failure (Ok/Err)

✅ Match must be **exhaustive** - handle all cases!

questions.question: What does Option<T>.None represent?
questions.explanation: None represents the absence of a value, a safe alternative to null.

questions.question: What happens if you don't handle all enum variants in a match?
questions.explanation: BPL requires exhaustive matching - you must handle all variants or use _ wildcard.

questions.question: In Result<int, string>, what does the string represent?
questions.explanation: Result<T, E> has success type T (int) and error type E (string).
